title: A Standardized On-Chip Communication Interface for Dynamic Hardware/Software Task Migration in Heterogeneous SoPCs
content: systems-on-programmable-chip combine processors and reconfigurable logic, but task communication can remain coupled to the current placement of neighboring tasks. This paper presents an architecture-level communication contract for dynamic hardware/software task migration. Software and hardware adapters expose a common logical task namespace, while cooperating managers configure routes, manage explicit state buffers, and coordinate local mailboxes. The migration specification distinguishes quiescence, state preservation, route rebinding, partial-bitstream loading, and resumption, with explicit cache and buffer ownership responsibilities. An analytical evaluation examines interface-variant counts, transport-cycle budgets, mailbox preservation, and configuration-transfer sensitivity. Under an illustrative effective drain rate of 800 MB/s and a fixed overhead of 1 microsecond, preserving 1-64 KiB requires 2.28-82.92 microseconds in the model. These values exclude unmodeled quiescence and state-restoration costs and are not board measurements. The accompanying code reproduces the calculations and records their assumptions. The contribution is a reproducible architectural specification and cost decomposition, rather than a validated implementation or a claim of performance superiority. A prospective validation protocol identifies the measurements needed to establish correctness, resource use, and end-to-end migration downtime on a CPU/FPGA platform.
